title: Source-based example — Revolution of the Earth
source_example: Revolution is the motion of an object around another object.
explanation: While rotating on its own axis, the Earth also revolves around the Sun as we learnt in Grade 6.

title: Source-based example — Changing view of night sky from the Earth
source_example: We know that this occurs due to the Earth’s rotation.
explanation: Every evening the Sun sets in the westward direction and the night sky becomes visible.

title: Source-based example — Seasons on the Earth
source_example: Is it related to the revolution of the Earth around the Sun in some way? I have also noticed that days are longer in summer than in winter.
explanation: I have noticed that we go through a cycle of seasons every year.

title: Source-based example — Eclipses
source_example: Could the light from the Sun get blocked by the two planets which are revolving between the Earth and the Sun? The planets Mercury and Venus appear very small compared to the Sun, and never block the entire light from the Sun reaching us.

title: Source-based example — Solar eclipse
source_example: You may wonder how the Moon, which is smaller than the Sun, blocks the light coming from the Sun that we see in the sky.
explanation: At certain times, the Moon can come in between the Sun and the Earth in a way that obstructs the light from the Sun from reaching us.

title: Source-based example — Lunar eclipse
source_example: On such days, we see the Earth’s shadow falling on the full disc of the Moon.
explanation: As the Moon revolves around the Earth, sometimes the Earth can block the sunlight from reaching the Moon.
